column1: # Per-assembly line-coverage floors, BY PROFILE.
# ⚠️ A `ci` NUMBER MUST COME FROM A CI RUN. NOT FROM A DEV MACHINE.
# This file shipped with a `ci` floor of 0.76 for Excise.Rendering and turned
# CI red for four consecutive commits, because that number was measured on a
# developer machine. Applying CI's test FILTER locally does not reproduce CI's
# ENVIRONMENT, and the environment is the entire reason this file has profiles
# at all. Measured on Excise.Rendering, same filter, same 467-odd tests:
#     CI runner (corpus-less)        54.36%      86 of 468 tests SKIP
#     dev machine, CI filter         78.41%       0 of 467 tests skip
# The 86 are corpus- and tool-gated tests living in classes the filter does not
# exclude by name. They do not announce themselves as filtered out; they run,
# hit a missing corpus, and skip. So the local run looks like the CI run, is
# named like the CI run, and measures 24 points higher.
# To get a `ci` number: read it off a CI run's "Coverage Report for package X"
# line. Not from `dotnet test` on your laptop, however carefully you copy the
# filter out of ci.yml.
# WHY TWO PROFILES
# Excise.Rendering, three populations, three numbers:
#     ci    corpus-less runner, filtered           54.36%
#     (dev machine w/ CI's filter — NOT A PROFILE) 78.41%
#     full  corpora + mutool/gs/pdftocairo, all    87.49%
# The ci -> full gap is TWO mechanisms, and an earlier version of this file
# attributed all of it to the second:
#   1. 54.36 -> 78.41   tests that SKIP on a corpus-less runner (invisible)
#   2. 78.41 -> 87.49   Corpus/Differential/Benchmark/Visual, excluded by name
# A single floor is wrong in both directions:
#   * set at 87% -> CI fails on every run, forever
#   * set at 54% for the release read -> a regression that only shows in the
#                 differential tests passes silently, and those are the tests
#                 that exist because excise must not be its own oracle
# This mirrors the skip-allowlist's environment conditioning (#854), which
# exists for the same reason: the allowlist is calibrated for a corpus-LESS
# runner, and entries declare what they need in order to run. That this file
# cited #854 and then made exactly the mistake #854 describes is the reason for
# the warning at the top.
# HOW FLOORS ARE CHOSEN
# ~2 points below the measured value. Tight enough to catch a real regression,
# loose enough not to flap. The `ci` value is safe to set tight because
# check-skip-budget.sh pins the CI skip set in BOTH directions — which is why
# 54.36% is stable to four significant figures across four separate runs. If
# the skip set moves, that gate fails first and names the cause.
# Floors RATCHET UP as coverage improves; they do not drift down. Raising one is
# a normal part of improving coverage. Lowering one requires saying why in the
# commit message — and "the old number was never measured in the environment it
# gates" is a correction, not a reduction.
# THE RATCHET IS MECHANICAL, NOT ASPIRATIONAL (#909)
#     scripts/check-coverage-floor.sh <report> <profile> <assembly> --update
# raises the floor when coverage improved materially, keeping ~2 points of
# headroom, and rewrites the `measured` column either way so this file records
# what was last observed. Three rules, each enforced by
# scripts/test-check-coverage-floor.sh in t0:
#   * it NEVER lowers — a regression exits non-zero and leaves this file
#     untouched. A ratchet that rewrites the floor to match a drop would launder
#     exactly the regressions it exists to catch.
#   * it ignores marginal gains, so run-to-run wobble cannot tighten a floor
#     until it flaps.
#   * it keeps headroom, matching how the hand-chosen floors were set.
# Before this, "ratchet" meant "floor": protected against decline, no credit for
# improvement, and the gap widening silently until the gate guarded a number
# nobody had met in months.
# THE FAILURE MODE TO WATCH
# `ci` is enforced on every push, so it gets attention. `full` is read by the
# release path (docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md) as an OBSERVATION, not a blocker, and
# is read far less often — so `full` is where rot hides. If `full` and `ci` ever
# converge, that is not coverage improving; it is the differential tests having
# stopped contributing, and it should be investigated rather than celebrated.
# NO FLOOR IS BETTER THAN A WRONG ONE
# Excise.App, Excise.Avalonia and Excise.Ocr had `ci` rows here produced by the
# same invalid local measurement. Nothing enforced them, so nothing caught it.
# They are DELETED rather than corrected: check-coverage-floor.sh fails on an
# undeclared pair, so wiring one of those gates now stops loudly and demands a
# CI-measured number, instead of silently passing against a figure that was
# never true. Re-add them by reading a CI run, one at a time, as each is wired.
# Format:  profile <TAB> assembly <TAB> floor <TAB> measured <TAB> note
# `measured` is the observation the floor was derived from — record where it
# came from in the note.
ci
